literal: Word humility from enemies do not accept; bow bending harm because of intending.
translation: Do not accept the humble words of your enemies; the bending of a bow is only for bringing about harm.
modern: பகைவர்களிடம் காணப்படும் பணிவான சொற்களை நம்பி ஏற்றுக்கொள்ளக் கூடாது; ஏனெனில், வில் வளைவது தீமை செய்வதற்காகவே ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet warns us not to trust the polite or submissive words of an enemy. The poet uses a brilliant double meaning of the word 'vaṇakkam', which means both 'humility' (in speech) and 'bending' (of an object). Just as the bending of a bow is not a sign of respect but a preparation to shoot a lethal arrow, the humble speech of an adversary is merely a prelude to causing harm. Therefore, one must remain vigilant and not be deceived by superficial sweetness.
